item.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
item.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterm: Democrats Retake Senate In Major Blow Against Trump’s Republican
item.description: Democrats won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout Tuesday with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. item.title: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit on Tuesday in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Power, logistics and so on and so forth.” She added that Nigeria needed to move beyond its domestic market and develop the capacity to supply other African countries. Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. item.title: ADC vows to proceed with Sokoto campaign despite intimidation
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to proceed with its scheduled campaign in Sokoto State despite what it described as attempts by the state government to intimidate the opposition and obstruct its political activities. The party also warned that Governor Ahmed Aliyu would be held responsible if any violence was directed at opposition members or supporters in the state. The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday, accusing the Sokoto State Government of undermining democratic rights and deliberately frustrating the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdullahi said the party would not be deterred by the alleged intimidation, insisting that no governor had the authority to prevent any political party from campaigning or presenting its candidates to voters. “The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership. Public office is a temporary mandate from the people, not a licence to suppress political competition,” the statement read. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.” The ADC spokesperson called on the state government to immediately stop what he described as efforts to frustrate its lawful political activities and guarantee a level playing field for all political parties. He also reminded security agencies and other public institutions that their responsibility was to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, rather than the political interests of the ruling party. Abdullahi warned that public officials who abused their authority to obstruct lawful political activities would face the legal consequences of their actions. “Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria simply because those in power are afraid of political competition,” he said. He maintained that democratic participation was a constitutional right and not a privilege to be granted by elected public officials. The ADC spokesperson further accused the ruling party of displaying intolerance towards opposition activities, challenging it to submit itself to an open contest if it believed it had performed well in government. item.title: Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan The pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, has risen to N1,370 per litre in Lagos, following fresh increases in depot prices across major supply locations. Checks by Vanguard on Tuesday showed that MRS and NNPC filling stations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while Mobil sold at N1,349. Some independent marketers sold at between N1,365 and N1,370, depending on location. The increase followed sharp movements in depot prices, particularly in Lagos, where A.A. Rano raised its PMS price by N75 to N1,295 per litre, while African Terminal, Aiteo and Integrated increased their prices to about N1,300. NIPCO also raised its price by N55 to N1,305, while Dangote’s price edged up by N3 to N1,303. MRS retained its depot price at N1,310. In Port Harcourt, Matrix increased its PMS price by N15 to N1,300 per litre, while Bulk Strategic, Masters and T.S.L remained at N1,300. Warri also recorded increases, with A.Y.M. Shafa and Matrix raising their prices by N17 each to N1,300, while Parker moved up by N15 to the same level. Calabar recorded higher PMS prices, with Fynefield and Northwest at N1,360 per litre. Meanwhile, Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, recorded mixed movements. In Lagos, WOSBAB cut its AGO price by N21 to N1,809 per litre, while Bulk Strategic reduced its price by N15 to N1,835. Rain Oil and Dangote also reduced their prices to N1,850 and N1,823 respectively. In Warri, Matrix and Rain Oil cut their AGO prices by N5 each to N1,835 per litre, while Edo Refinery, NIPCO and Prudent retained theirs at N1,840. The latest figures point to continued volatility in the downstream market as changes in depot prices filter through to retail outlets. “To safeguard port integrity and vessel safety, all maritime operators, terminal users, and personnel must utilise authorised reporting protocols immediately upon detecting any security incident or anomaly,” the agency stated. item.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. item.title: Nigeria’s exports record 25% increase in 2yrs — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s exports have increased by 25 per cent in the last two years, driven by Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port terminal operators, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has said. Speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH), Dantsoho said the growth covered both oil and non-oil exports. “For us in Nigeria, the most important thing is that we are seeing growth as a result of this policy that we are taking. Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. “These are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In manufacturing and agriculture, raw materials like cocoa and cashew, volumes have increased, and that is to the credit of the partnership between ourselves and the major terminal operators, APM Terminals,” he said. He attributed the improvement to Export Processing Terminals established by the NPA. “We have got about four of those in Nigeria where we collaborate with the terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies that have a stake, so that everything regarding the processing of cargo for export is done locally,” he stated. On the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Dantsoho said: “Nigeria’s economy is very strong now because of our president’s reforms, which everyone can testify is attracting investors to the country.” He added that port reforms had improved operational efficiency and increased revenue. “We have experienced a lot of increase in volumes and revenue that has been generated by the ports across Nigeria. As a matter of fact, the efficiency in the ports in Nigeria is far better now than those of other West African countries,” he said. Dantsoho also disclosed that the Federal Government was investing $1 billion in expanding and modernising Apapa Port, with private-sector partnerships supporting infrastructure and technology development. item.title: US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats
item.description: United States President Donald Trump has said he is prepared to accept the outcome of the country’s midterm elections and work with Democrats, as results showed the opposition party heading towards control of both chambers of Congress. Trump made the remarks on Tuesday night during a telephone interview with The New York Times, as he monitored election results at the White House. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said. “We’ll probably work something out.” The President’s comments came amid major Republican losses, with Democrats making significant gains in closely contested races and threatening Republican control of Congress. Trump attributed his party’s poor performance partly to his absence from the ballot, suggesting that his participation could have changed the outcome. He also defended his decision to launch a war against Iran, describing it as a “very wise decision”. The President further said he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, including South Carolina Senator Darline Graham and Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton, who both lost their Senate bids. Speaking shortly before 10:30pm on Tuesday, Trump said he was following the election results during the interview. “I’m just looking at these results as I’m talking,” he said. Reacting to Graham’s defeat, he added: “I see that Darline lost. Wow, that’s amazing. How do you think Lindsey would have done if he ran?” He was referring to Senator Lindsey Graham, who reportedly died in July. Democrats were on course to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate as results continued to emerge, PUNCH Online had reported on Wednesday. A Democratic takeover of Congress would significantly alter the balance of political power in Washington, potentially subjecting Trump’s administration to increased congressional scrutiny and making it more difficult for the President to advance his legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. item.title: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Sokoto State Government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and frustrate its political activities, following the sealing of its state campaign office in Sokoto. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. item.title: LG reinforces leadership in refrigerator market with Brandcom award
item.description: LG Electronics has strengthened its position in Nigeria’s home appliance market following the recognition of its MoodUP Refrigerator at the BRANDCOM awards 2026 in Lagos. The award recognises the refrigerator’s distinctive design and smart features, including customisable LED door panels and smart connectivity, which allow users to personalise their kitchen experience. Beyond its aesthetics, LG’s refrigerator range addresses practical household needs such as food preservation, energy efficiency and durability, which remain important considerations for Nigerian consumers. The company offers top-freezer, bottom-freezer, side-by-side and premium refrigerator models designed to accommodate different household sizes and lifestyles. One of its products, the GN-F452PFAQ Top Freezer Refrigerator, features FRESH Converter+ technology, which allows users to adjust temperature settings to suit different food types and maintain optimal freshness. It also comes with an automatic ice maker for added convenience. Selected LG refrigerator models are equipped with Smart Inverter Compressor , LINEARCooling and DoorCooling+ technologies, designed to improve energy efficiency, provide consistent cooling and preserve food freshness for longer. These features are particularly relevant to households seeking reliable refrigeration, lower energy consumption and dependable appliance performance. The recognition at the BRANDCOM Awards further highlights LG’s presence in Nigeria’s competitive refrigerator market. item.title: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals
item.description: MACKINAW CITY — Mackinaw City will play for an MHSAA Division 4 district volleyball title . Taking on Mackinac Island in a district semifinal , the Comets booked their ticket to a championship clash at St. Ignace by capturing a 3-0 victory (25-12, 25-11, 25-16) over the Lakers in Mackinaw City on Tuesday, Nov. 3. MACK CITY'S RIAN ESPER: Esper a key Mackinaw City volleyball player in many different spots MACK CITY BOYS QUALIFY FOR XC STATES: Area's top performers paced by state-qualifier Mackinaw City boys XC DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments After starting slow and trailing 7-1 in the first set, the Comets (13-22-5) regrouped, battled back and took a one-set lead in the match. From there, they were in cruise control behind quality offensive and defensive play. "Once we were able to get ourselves settled, we played some very solid volleyball tonight and did a great job of getting into our system offensively, and our defense did a great job of digging balls and keeping balls alive to give ourselves a shot at winning some long volleys," Mackinaw City coach Jake Huffman said. Rian Esper's 10 kills, six aces and six digs fueled the Comets, who received 16 assists, seven digs, two kills and seven digs from Julia Short, and 11 digs, six assists, four kills and three aces from Emily Kruczynski. Mackinaw City's many other contributors included Alaia Mendez (eight kills, five aces, four digs), Poppy Wallace (five kills, two digs, one block), Ella Kruczynski (six aces, five digs, one assist), and Sarah Lentell (two kills, one dig). "I was very happy with our response and proud of the effort that ladies put forth tonight," Huffman said. "We will use (Wednesday) to prep for a very tough St. Ignace squad on Thursday." Thursday's district final at St. Ignace (10-11-7) is a 6 p.m. start. item.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole. Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women’s basketball team on the Hawkeyes. Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women’s basketball team Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift. The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players’ feet during the game. While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue. The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark’s final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists. Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich’s 54-year-old 3,667-point record. She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season. Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball. item.title: REFORMS: Oil output has grown by 600,000bpd since PIA — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s crude oil production has increased by 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), from about 1.2 million bpd to 1.8 million bpd, following the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) and reforms in the oil and gas sector, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has said. Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bashir Bayo Ojulari, disclosed this yesterday at the 2026 Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Speaking at an Energy Talk titled, “Nigeria’s Reform Agenda: Competing for Energy Capital,” Ojulari attributed the production increase to the implementation of the PIA 2021, improved investment climate, better investment decisions and stronger collaboration between NNPC and its partners. He said the company was working towards achieving Nigeria’s two million bpd production ambition by 2027 through improved maintenance of existing infrastructure, protection of base production, increased output from producing assets and execution of new projects. “The figure of 1.8 million barrels per day is a stage in a journey towards our objective. We are concentrating on the basics, which are maintaining our infrastructure, protecting base operations and executing the projects that will take production higher,” he said. On domestic energy supply, the NNPC boss said the removal of petrol subsidy had been accompanied by a major compressed natural gas (CNG) programme, with more than 400 conversion centres established across the country. He added that over 1,000 trucks used in transporting petroleum products had also been converted to run on CNG. Ojulari disclosed that the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline was completed in August 2026, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline was expected to deliver gas to Abuja before the end of the year to support power generation, data centres and industrial hubs. On gas development, he said NNPC was targeting national production of 10 billion standard cubic feet per day (Bscf/d) by 2027 and 12 Bscf/d by 2030, supported by the development of domestic and international markets. He also said the countries involved in the Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline had aligned and executed the necessary agreements, while Nigeria, Algeria and Niger had reached alignment on the development of the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline. On investment, Ojulari cited major projects, including TotalEnergies’ Ubeta, Shell’s Bonga South-West and Eni’s Zabazaba developments, noting that commercial agreements covering about $20 billion in investments had been concluded. He added that NNPC was building new relationships with international partners, including the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and Chinese investors in Nigeria’s refineries, while working with global oilfield service companies to expand capacity in the country. item.title: US Midterms: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans
item.description: Democrats have taken control of both chambers of the United States Congress in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory marks a significant shift in the balance of power in Washington, giving Democrats control of the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency. According to the BBC, Democrats had secured a majority in the House of Representatives as of Wednesday, although vote counting was continuing in several states. The figures available at the time of filing this report showed Democrats with 194 seats in the House against 115 for Republicans, while in the Senate, Democrats had secured 52 seats against 40 for Republicans. The Democratic Party also recorded major upsets in several closely contested Senate races, winning Republican-held seats in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, while retaining Democratic seats in Georgia and New Hampshire. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton, becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in the state since 1988. In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham, becoming the first woman elected to the US Senate from the state and the first Democrat to win a Senate seat there in more than two decades. Democrat Roy Cooper also defeated Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina, while Sherrod Brown defeated Republican incumbent Jon Husted to win the Ohio Senate race. The results represent a major reversal of political fortunes for Republicans, whose control of Congress had given Trump’s administration considerable legislative advantage. The midterm elections, held on Tuesday, November 3, determine the composition of the United States Congress, comprising the 435-member House of Representatives and the 100-member Senate. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats were contested. The Democratic takeover is expected to intensify congressional scrutiny of Trump’s administration, with the opposition party gaining control of key committees and greater powers to investigate government policies and decisions. The BBC reported that Democratic control of the House could significantly constrain what Trump could achieve during the remaining two years of his presidency. Democrats could launch investigations into the president and his family, as well as controversial decisions and policies of his administration. Reacting to the Republican losses, Trump sought to distance himself from the outcome, arguing that his absence from the ballot contributed to the party’s poor performance. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he wrote on his Truth Social platform. However, in an interview with The New York Times published later, Trump said he was prepared to accept the election results and work with Democrats. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. item.title: NESG: Economic growth must deliver jobs, higher incomes
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Chairman of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), Mr. Omoboyede Olusanya, has called for a shift from measuring Nigeria’s economic progress by headline growth figures to delivering tangible improvements in jobs, incomes, productivity and living standards. Olusanya made the call at the closing of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) in Abuja, saying: “Growth that delivers is growth whose impact is strongly felt. “It means farmers earn more because their productivity has improved; manufacturers produce at lower cost; graduates find decent jobs; businesses access affordable financing; and children receive the nutrition and healthcare they need to thrive.” Introducing “Growth that Delivers” as the guiding principle of his tenure as NESG chairman, he said: “While recent reforms have helped restore macroeconomic stability, stability is only the starting point. “Bridging the distance between macroeconomic stability and accelerated growth, and between accelerated growth and improved lives and livelihoods, is the task before us all.” Outlining his priorities, Olusanya pledged to make accountability a central feature of the organisation’s engagement with government and other stakeholders. “We will ensure that every priority commitment from this Summit has a designated owner, a timeline and measurable indicators of success, building on the NES Accountability Framework and publishing progress ahead of NES#33,” he stated. On evidence-driven policy, he said: “We will strengthen our research and policy intelligence to produce rigorous, practical and costed recommendations linked to the National Development Plan 2026–2030.” On investment mobilisation, he pledged that the NESG would work with government, financial institutions and development partners to “turn policy ideas into bankable projects and mobilise capital into agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure, technology, entrepreneurship and skills.” He also promised to expand economic opportunities across all regions and states, with greater attention to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and the informal economy. On institutional sustainability, he said the NESG would broaden its membership, increase the participation of women and young people, protect its independence and strengthen its sustainability for future generations. Calling for collective action, Olusanya urged governments at all levels to “sustain and improve reforms, reduce the costs of power, logistics and doing business, and maintain predictable policies backed by clear, measurable commitments.” He challenged private-sector leaders to “invest, innovate, develop workforce skills, pay fairly and create productive jobs.” He also urged young Nigerians to “build enterprises, acquire relevant skills and hold institutions accountable,” while calling on civil society to monitor commitments and amplify the voices of underserved communities. item.title: Emiliano Martínez, Valentín Barco, Aarón Anselmino called up by Argentina
item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez during the Premier League match between Everton and Chelsea at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images There’s an international break after this weekend’s matches, but for a fair few Chelsea boys, there will be no rest. And among those set for national team duty are our trio or Argentinians. Trio? — you might ask. Who all could that be? After all, Enzo Fernández is gone. Alejandro Garnacho is gone. And Emi Martínez has a broken face. Who’s left? Valentín Barco. Sure. Get in the chopper! But joining Barco are indeed Martínez, and, in an even bigger surprise, Aarón Anselmino — man with no actual minutes of competitive senior football yet this season. Maybe Argentina just want their own Estêvão situation. Argentina are playing only a couple friendlies during this break, against Uruguay and Costa Rica, and manager Lionel Scaloni is using this opportunity to check out some fresh faces. Anselmino is one of two players called up with zero senior caps, and one of nine with less than five. (Barco himself is barely above that threshold at seven.) And Emi’s inclusion is hopefully a good sign that is recovery from the fractured jaw he suffered against Everton a few weeks ago is going well. item.title: “The Legacy Continues”: 2Baba Announces New Album ‘Oldest Young Man’
item.description: 2Baba wearing a hooded black pleated drape and sunglasses to announce his studio album, Oldest Young Man. Afrobeats icon 2Baba is officially returning with a full-length body of work, and November 27 is the date to mark in your calendars! The legendary singer and songwriter—formerly known as 2Face Idibia —took to Instagram to announce his upcoming studio album, titled Oldest Young Man. Taking to social media to share the exciting release date, the Afropop veteran captioned his post: The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date. The announcement marks a huge moment for African music fans. Oldest Young Man is 2Baba’s first studio album in over six years, following his critically acclaimed 2020 project, Warriors , which featured heavyweights like Burna Boy , Wizkid , and Olamide . While he hasn’t dropped a full-length album since then, the Nigerian music pioneer has remained active with steady releases, most recently dropping singles like “ Mental ” in September 2026 and “ Ifesinachi ” earlier in the year. With over two decades at the top of the game—stretching from his days with Plantashun Boiz to solo anthems like “ African Queen “—the legend is set to prove once again why his sound stands the test of time. Oldest Young Man arrives on all streaming platforms on 27 November 2026. 2Baba posing in a draped black pleated outfit and black sunglasses ahead of his upcoming album, Oldest Young Man. *** Photo Credit: 2Baba/Instagram The post “The Legacy Continues”: 2Baba Announces New Album ‘Oldest Young Man’ appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Viola Station 107: The more things change
item.description: We’re sticking our necks out a bit with some of these takes. | Jacob King/PA Images via Getty Images So full disclosure: we recorded this before the Sassuolo game . And our collective emotional state was considerably lower. We were, in fact, struggling with our feelings. The podcast reflects that because, in hindsight, we were a little bit grim about Fiorentina’s prospects going forward. That’s apparent in pretty much everything we discussed. What did we discuss? Well, we ran through the recent history, picking our standouts (big dogs, boneheads, et cetera) before considering some tactical and statistical stuff which, in hindsight, probably doesn’t matter as much after Fiorentina got its wait a minute second? That can’t be right, can it? Second win of the season? Okay, yeah, maybe we weren’t entirely wrong in being ruffled. That Relegation Percent-O-Meter still resembles the Doomsday Clock. On the plus side, we got a wonderful McMike milestone, some unexpectedly terse Producer Mike analysis, and Tito completely failing to throw to an advertisement correctly. item.title: Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nikita Kucherov wants out of the Tampa Bay Lightning , but he still can’t stop going all out for his team. Reports surfaced last Friday that the 33-year-old Kucherov had already asked the Lightning to move him. In the two games since, the two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner has done nothing on the ice but rack up points. Against the Nashville Predators on Saturday on the road, Kucherov had a hand in three of his team’s goals, as he recorded a trio of assists, albeit in a 5-4 shootout loss to Steven Stamkos and company. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bolts returned to action on Tuesday, and Kucherov was clearly still feeling it, adding two more assists to his total in the 2026-27 NHL season. This time around, his effort did not go for naught, with the Lightning defeating the Detroit Red Wings, 4-2. Kucherov is in a contract year, which means he is on track to become a free agent next summer. However, he also clarified that his trade request is less about money and more about the perceived disrespect he feels from Tampa Bay over its “poor communication.” It remains to be seen how this saga between Kucherov and the Lightning will conclude, but what seems to be clear is that he is not shortchanging the only team he’s played for so far in his NHL career when it comes to his effort and production on the ice. Kucherov and the Lightning improved to 9-3-2 after the win against Detroit. Up next for them is a date with the visiting Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. item.title: Ex-Broncos QB Russell Wilson Interviewed for FBS Head Coaching Job
item.description: Denver Broncos head coach Russell Wilson. Getty Former Denver Broncos quarterback Russell Wilson could be headed for a major career shift less than one year after the end of his NFL career. “Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, ” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on Tuesday night. “Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. NC State fired Dave Doeren as head coach on Oct. 24. Wilson played at NC State from 2008 to 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin in 2011. After being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft, he went on to play 14 seasons in the NFL, leading the Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.” Wilson, a 10-time NFL All-Pro, retired in June and has been working for CBS Sports as an analyst this fall. “Interesting that Russell Wilson and Philip Rivers are contenders,” NFL reporter Ed Werder wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. Wilson spent his first 10 seasons with the Seattle Seahawks , where he won one Super Bowl and played in another before a blockbuster trade to the Broncos before the 2022 season. He lasted 2 seasons in Denver before spending one season each with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Giants . Broncos’ Wilson Trade One of NFL’s All-Time Worst Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox called the Broncos’ trade with the Seahawks for Wilson “Worst NFL Trade of the Last 10 Years” for the franchise. By releasing Wilson in April 2024, the Broncos were forced to take an NFL-record $85 million dead cap hit spread across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. “The Denver Broncos’ ill-fated 2022 trade for Russell Wilson has largely been overshadowed by the disastrous deal Cleveland made for Deshaun Watson in the same offseason,” Knox wrote. “However, that doesn’t mean that Denver’s deal was a good one. In fact, the Wilson trade might be considered the worst of the last decade if not for the Watson debacle. The Broncos coughed up two first-round picks, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick, quarterback Drew Lock , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and tight end Noah Fant to acquire Wilson and a fourth-round pick. The Broncos then signed Wilson to an extension worth $242.6 million over five years with $161 million guaranteed.” Russell Wilson, Sean Payton Butted Heads in 2023 The writing was on the wall for Wilson once Nathaniel Hackett was fired after one season as Denver’s head coach in 2022 and replaced with former New Orleans Saints head coach and Super Bowl champion Sean Payton. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson rejuvenated his career somewhat in 2024 with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a 1-year, $1.2 million contract. item.title: Ziaire Williams gets candid on ‘easy’ role alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Ziaire Williams gets candid on ‘easy’ role alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers ’ current win streak hit two games following their 138-117 thrashing of the Miami Heat on Monday, and the team welcomed the return of forward Ziaire Williams. The six-year veteran had been sidelined for three games due to a foot injury , but he was cleared to go, picking up right where he left off prior to sitting out. Although Ziaire Williams had been in the starting lineup to begin the season, he came off the Lakers’ bench in the win against the Heat, contributing nine points on 3-of-6 shooting from the 3-point line. Williams has been one of the team’s most dependable 3&D players , along with Matisse Thybulle, and for him, the uptick in his shooting efficiency is due to the players he’s playing alongside. “They’re easy looks, way easier than they’ve been in the past. Like I said, they’re sending two to Luka [Doncic], two to AR [Austin Reaves] every time,” Williams said during his postgame press conference after the win against the Heat. “It’s just swing, swing, one more and I get to set my feet, get to square up the ball. I put a lot of work this summer. [I’m] trusting my work, confident in my shot, my shot feels great. I put the reps in, so I just got to trust it.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Through five games this season, Williams is shooting career-highs across the board. He’s up to 55.9 percent from the field and 46.7 percent from the 3-point line. His previous career-bests in shooting efficiency was 45 percent from the field and 34.3 percent from 3-point range. He’s right at his career averages in shot attempts as well with 6.8 overall field goal attempts and 4.2 3-point attempts. And he’s averaging a career-high in points with 10.8. Prior to his return from injury, his points per game average was 11.3. Williams’ production is key to the Lakers’ success, especially when it comes to playing off Doncic. Teams have begun to trap and blitz Doncic, and the Lakers haven’t done so well in responding to that type of defense in the early-goings of the season. But against the Heat, the team did a much better job at reacting and adjusting to the defense. While it’s still a work in progress, Williams believes the team has the right mentality and personnel to continue countering what opposing teams through at them defensively. “[It’s] a lot of good reps of practicing. They send two on the ball, there’s always going to be a 4-on-3 advantage on the back side. It’s just about countering on those advantages, looking opposite for corner threes, finishing at the rim,” Williams said. “The short roll is so important with those blitzes cause it opens up the floor for all of us. item.title: NC State Interviews Super Bowl Champion as Philip Rivers Gets Familiar Competition
item.description: 11 Nov 2001: Philip Rivers #17 of N.C.St. celebrates after his team won 34-28 during the Florida State -North Carolina State game at Doak Campell Stadium in Tallahassee , Fl.. DIGITAL IMAGE Mandatory Credit: Andy Lyons/ALLSPORT Getty RALEIGH, NC - SEPTEMBER 3: Quarterback Russell Wilson #16 of the North Carolina State Wolfpack drops back to pass against the South Carolina Gamecocks during the game at Carter-Finley Stadium on September 3, 2009 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Streeter Lecka/Getty Images) Getty The NC State Wolfpack could turn to a familiar quarterback to lead their next chapter, and Russell Wilson has now taken a step toward that possibility. According to ESPN insider Adam Schefter, Wilson interviewed for the program’s head coaching vacancy Tuesday. His involvement adds another recognizable name to a search that already includes Philip Rivers. For Wolfpack fans, the connection is obvious. Both quarterbacks starred at NC State before building lengthy NFL careers. Now, the program is considering whether that experience and familiarity could translate into leadership from the sideline. Russell Wilson Interviews for NC State Opening Wilson played three seasons for NC State from 2008 through 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin. He later led Seattle to a Super Bowl championship and became one of the NFL’s most recognizable quarterbacks. After retiring in June, he joined CBS Sports as an analyst. The reported interview introduces a different possibility for his next football chapter. Broadcasting allows Wilson to explain the game from outside the building. Coaching would require him to shape everything happening inside it, from player development to the staff responsible for executing his vision. Getty RALEIGH, NC – SEPTEMBER 3: Quarterback Russell Wilson #16 of the North Carolina State Wolfpack drops back to pass against the South Carolina Gamecocks during the game at Carter-Finley Stadium on September 3, 2009 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Streeter Lecka/Getty Images) That distinction should guide the conversation around his candidacy. Playing quarterback at an elite level provides insight into preparation, leadership and offensive football. Running a college program adds recruiting, roster management and organizational responsibilities that demand their own evaluation. Wilson’s history gives him a compelling story to tell prospective players. The question for NC State is how he would support that message with experienced assistants and a sustainable plan. An interview gives the school an opportunity to examine those details. Philip Rivers Adds Another Familiar Option Rivers brings a different background to the discussion. He has coached at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama since 2021, providing experience leading a team after his playing career. ESPN reported that he wants to finish the current high school season. That experience does not eliminate the adjustment involved in taking over a college program. Howev

item.title: Fan Favorite ‘The Iron Turtle’ Returns at UFC Saudi Arabia
item.description: JunYong Park UFC Saudi Arabia Getty Fan favorite middleweight JunYong Park, nicknamed “The Iron Turtle,” will make his return to the Octagon at UFC Saudi Arabia. The UFC Saudi Arabia card takes place on Saturday, December 5, at ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and is rumored to be headlined by a five-round middleweight matchup between strikers Israel Adesanya and Shara Magomedov. JunYong Park vs. Marco Tulio Added to UFC Saudi Arabia Per AG Fight, Park will fight Marco Tulio at UFC Saudi Arabia. Heavy.com’s Marcel Dorff has confirmed the bout will take place at UFC Saudi Arabia. View this post on Instagram JunYong Park Is a UFC Fan Favorite The 35-year-old Park first joined the UFC in 2019, and since then he has racked up a 9-4 record inside the Octagon, with notable wins over Ismail Naurdiev, Brad Tavares, and Marc-Andre Barriault. Park has not competed yet in 2026, as his last fight was a unanimous decision defeat to Ikram Aliskerov at UFC 321 in October 2025. Despite that loss, Park is still a very solid fighter and a tough out at 185 lbs, as he is a durable fighter with a really good ground game and passable striking. The Iron Turtle bustin’ the moves! 🕺 🇰🇷Jun Yong Park caps off his four-fight win streak with a celebratory dance! Who should he face next after #UFCVegas77 ? pic.twitter.com/BDPUkgc4Et — UFC_Asia (@UFC_Asia) July 17, 2023 In this matchup at UFC Saudi Arabia, Park will take on Tulio, the Brazilian knockout artist who is 2-2 in the UFC since joining the organization in 2025 after two wins on Dana White’s Contender Series to earn his UFC contract. Tulio won his first two UFC fights by knockout over Ihor Potieria and Tresean Gore, but he has fallen on hard times as of late with back-to-back losses against Christian Leroy Duncan and Roman Kopylov. Despite those two recent defeats, however, Tulio is not to be underestimated, as he is a powerful knockout artist who just needs to land one big punch, and he can put his opponents out cold. Overall, Park vs. Tulio should be a great fight, and one that is a true clash of styles, as Park will surely look to take the fight to the ground while Tulio will try to keep it standing. Therefore, the winner will likely be the fighter who can take the bout into their own realm and keep it there. item.title: Kochetkov suffers first loss as Predators down Hurricanes 4-1
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 03: Juuse Saros #74 of the Nashville Predators saves a shot on goal by Jordan Martinook #48 of the Carolina Hurricanes during the second period of the game at Bridgestone Arena on November 03, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Eventually the Hurricanes were going to lose again. One of the biggest truisms in the NHL is that good goaltending will beat just about anyone, especially on any given night. For the Hurricanes, Juuse Saros is on the list of players who just manage to elevate to a different level when they are across the ice. It happened again Tuesday Night as he made 29 saves in a 4-1 Nashville win over Carolina. On the other side, Pyotr Kochetkov did what he could to keep Carolina into the game, but his 16 saves were not enough as frustration mounted and despite dominating the first period Carolina went into the locker room down 1-0. Nick Perbix was the one who got the party started in Music City late in the first, as Nashville had one of their few sustained pressure sessions of the period. They didn’t waste it as Filip Forsberg was able to jar the puck away from Sean Walker, and feed a perfect pass over to Perbix for the shot. Perbix used the traffic in front of the net to blast it by Kochetkov, and while Rod Brind’Amour called his timeout to try and see if the play were either offside or there should have been a high stick stoppage, he ultimately let it go. Forsberg would figure into the second goal in the next period, this time on a rush Nashville was able to get it deep and Forsberg would keep the puck from going out at the blue line. He feathered a great pass over to an open Roman Josi to give Nashville a 2-0 lead. Carolina would claw one back a few minutes later, though, as the white-hot Jackson Blake wouldn’t be denied. Blake would pass ahead over to a rushing Shayne Gostisbehere, and as he went in on Saros he passed it back to Blake who took one shot and then immediately roofed the rebound to claw Carolina back to 2-1. View Link That unfortunately would be the high point of the night for Carolina as while they would win the third period on shots 12-8, they couldn’t generate much of anything offensively. Kochetkov made several huge stops in the period to keep it close, but about five minutes in, he was unable to stop a great deflection by Adam Edstrom. Josi would peel back to the blue line and put on a shot that was about crest-level to Edstrom. Edstrom took his stick and deflected it back down to where Kochetkov couldn’t recover. The league checked the height of the stick and Brind’Amour wouldn’t challenge the call. Carolina would get a few chances with the empty net, but ultimately Ross Colton would get in all alone—with Brady Skjei and Jack Drury each getting a point versus their old teammates for good measure. item.title: Former Steelers QB Russell Wilson Interviews for NC State Coaching Job
item.description: BALTIMORE, MD - JANUARY 11: Russell Wilson #3 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to pass against the Baltimore Ravens during the first half of the AFC Wild Card Playoff game at M&T Bank Stadium on January 11, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers‘ former quarterback Russell Wilson might be headed back to the college game, this time with a headset instead of a helmet. Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching vacancy at NC State, where he starred before finishing his college career at Wisconsin. The possibility comes just months after the former Steelers starter moved from the NFL field to the CBS broadcast desk, and he isn’t the only familiar quarterback in the running. Former Steelers QB Russell Wilson Interviews for NC State Job ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Nov. 3 that Wilson met with NC State about succeeding Dave Doeren. “Sources: former Super Bowl champion QB Russell Wilson interviewed today for the head coaching job at North Carolina State, where he played three seasons,” Schefter wrote. Schefter also named fellow former Wolfpack quarterback Philip Rivers among the prominent candidates. Wilson has no college or NFL coaching experience, making the interview a considerable departure from his previous football roles. The 37-year-old played at NC State from 2008-10, throwing for 8,545 yards and 76 touchdowns. He became the first freshman quarterback named first-team All-ACC. After transferring to Wisconsin for his final college season in 2011, he went on to win a Super Bowl with Seattle and make 10 Pro Bowls. His Pittsburgh connection is much more recent. Wilson started 11 games for the Steelers in 2024, going 6-5 with 2,482 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and five interceptions. Pittsburgh reached the playoffs but lost its final five games, including a wild-card defeat to Baltimore. Wilson spent 2025 with the New York Giants before joining CBS Sports’ “The NFL Today” this year. He works alongside former Steelers coach Bill Cowher on the pregame show and took the broadcasting job only five months ago. An earlier move to television appeared to close his playing career. Coaching could bring him back to the sideline. Philip Rivers Competes With Russell Wilson for NC State Opening Wilson’s interview adds intrigue to a search already centered on Rivers, another former NFL quarterback who became a star in Raleigh. ESPN’s Mark Schlabach and Pete Thamel reported Oct. 31 that Rivers had entered serious discussions with NC State, though no agreement was close. Rivers has coached St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama since 2021 and reached the state semifinals the past two seasons. His son, quarterback Gunner Rivers, is committed to NC State. Asked about the opening, Rivers told AL.com, “NC State’s special to me,” while cautioning, “you never say never, but there’s nothing imminent.” NC State fired Doeren on Oct. 24 following a 3-4 start, ending a 14-season tenure with a school-record 98

item.title: Karl-Anthony Towns gets honest about how he can still be impactful during off nights
item.description: Karl-Anthony Towns gets honest about how he can still be impactful during off nights originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Karl-Anthony Towns has arguably been the New York Knicks ' best player this season. Despite the Knicks ' win over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday, Towns did not have the best shooting night. Towns shot 4-for-11 from the field, but he made sure to make an impact everywhere else. He only scored 11 points, but he grabbed 16 rebounds and dished out 5 assists. It was a testament to how impactful Towns can be when he is locked in. Karl-Anthony Towns on how he impacts the game beyond scoring During his heyday with the Minnesota Timberwolves , Towns was seen as one of the best offensive big men. He was already a tremendous player back then because of his limitless offensive arsenal. However, he has added to his game after joining the Knicks. With New York, Towns has become more of a multi-dimensional player. He still scores and rebounds at a high level, but he has become a solid defender while also becoming a playmaking hub for Mike Brown's system. MORE: Mike Brown dives into how he has challenged Karl-Anthony Towns to help the Knicks win Most people see Jalen Brunson as the star player for the Knicks, and rightfully so. However, Towns has also earned the distinction of being a star because of how impactful he can be with or without the scoring numbers. "You gotta impact winning every single day. I may not shoot the ball well every day, but I can damn sure impact winning every time I step on the court with this Knicks jersey on. It says a lot about this team to come off a championship & still find different ways to get better, to grow, to fight through adversity," Towns said after the Knicks' win over the Nets . The Knicks still have a losing record at 3-4, but they are on the right track. As defending champions, the Knicks have huge targets on their backs, and the players know it. Towns and the rest of the Knicks roster are ready to step up and help New York get back-to-back championships. item.title: ‘Enough With the Mannings,’ ‘We Want (Tony) Romo’ — NFL Fans React to Report Naming Peyton Manning ‘Top Choice’ to Replace Troy Aikman on MNF
item.description: Former NFL quarterback and analyst Peyton Manning, CBS sportscaster and former NFL quarterback Tony Romo, and ESPN's Troy Aikman. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have become a familiar pairing on Monday Night Football, but ESPN may soon have to plan for a booth without Aikman. Their partnership has faced questions amid stalled contract talks and reports of tension between the broadcasters. This has put the network’s next move under the spotlight, with Peyton Manning reportedly at the top of ESPN’s wish list. Fans Weigh In on Peyton Manning Potentially Replacing Troy Aikman According to Andrew Marchand of The Athletic, ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro considers Manning his top choice to replace Aikman. Pitaro is expected to approach the Hall of Fame quarterback about joining Buck in the main Monday Night Football booth. However, Marchand does not expect Manning to accept the offer, making Greg Olsen a more realistic candidate. Manning already has a long-term relationship with ESPN through Omaha Productions. His deal runs through 2034, covering the ManningCast, which he hosts with his brother Eli. The format gives both brothers control over their game selections and lets them work from home rather than follow the demanding travel schedule of a traditional broadcast crew. That arrangement could make a move to the main booth difficult, even if ESPN offers a lucrative contract. Manning has also turned down traditional broadcasting opportunities before. Olsen, meanwhile, currently serves as Fox Sports’ No. 2 game analyst after Tom Brady took over its lead position. Marchand and Puck’s John Ourand have both identified Olsen as the likely choice. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor As the report made its way to social media, one user questioned whether Manning would benefit from the move. He wrote , “Love Manning but he talks too fast and trips over his own words. Plus, this would be a step down and pay cut to what he’s already doing.” Another fan suggested a different former quarterback for the role. Tony Romo, CBS’ former lead analyst, also emerged as an option for viewers. One user shared his take, writing , “Romo would be my choice.” Another fan made that preference crystal clear, writing , “We want Romo.” Not everyone wants another Manning on a major NFL broadcast, it would appear. One viewer expressed frustration with his frequent media appearances while backing Olsen, writing , “I’m so tired of Peyton Manning everywhere on TV… Greg Olsen is a great choice as he’s not overexposed and annoying.” This opinion matched another fan’s preference for the former Carolina Panthers tight end. “Enough with the Mannings! Olsen is the one!” the user wrote . The search comes amid reports that Buck and Aikman could part ways after the 2026 season. Buck recently signed a six-year ESPN extension worth $108 million, while Aikman’s contract talks have stalled. If Aikman leaves, ESPN will need to find the right analyst for its lead NFL booth. item.title: ‘The right call’ – NBA fans agree with Luka Doncic’s technical foul being rescinded
item.description: Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images Luka Doncic received his second technical foul of the season against the Miami Heat, but fans think it’s only right that the call has been overturned. Luka Doncic and the referees famously don’t get along. The Los Angeles Lakers superstar is known for getting into it with them. Just last season, Doncic served a one-game suspension in March after picking up his 16th technical foul of the year. He has reached that mark in four seasons. Through the first eight games of this season, Luka has been relatively better behaved. He picked up one technical foul in the clash against the Golden State Warriors. He was whistled for a second during LA’s 138-117 win against the Miami Heat, but that has since been rescinded. NBA fans call out referee after Luka Doncic’s technical foul against the Miami Heat was rescinded In the second quarter during the Heat clash, Doncic expressively disagreed with a call by the referee. This immediately resulted in a technical foul. He was seen protesting the decision during the game as well, letting the official know that they wouldn’t have called that on any other star. On Tuesday night, it was revealed that the call was being overturned. Fans responded by showing their support for Luka and questioning the referee instead. “This is the right call, but does the ref just get away with it now?” one fan asked. “Omg he really is gonna be MVP this year, even his techs are getting rescinded!” another observed. “Since when is clapping tech-worthy, these refs have built-in Luka hate,” a third fan said. “Every year he gets a lot of techs rescinded, it is kinda telling how biased the officials are against him,” a fourth fan wrote. “I need the ref who did it to come to the front,” a comment read. “You should publish what corrective actions you take on these incompetent referees,” a sixth fan appealed to the NBA. Doncic has his fair share of critics and doubters, but it seems that the general consensus this time is that he was wronged by the official. Having a technical rescinded is good news for the Lakers star, although hopefully he won’t think of it as having an extra one in the bank. item.title: Jack Della Maddalena Turns Down UFC Sydney Offer, Targets April or May 2027 Return
item.description: The last couple of fights haven’t gone Jack Della Maddalena’s way. The Australian is currently on a two-fight losing streak after dropping the welterweight title to Islam Makhachev at UFC 322 in November 2025 . Things got even worse in his next outing, as Carlos Prates dominated him before finishing the fight in the third round at UFC Perth. While fans were hoping to see Maddalena return on home soil at UFC Sydney on February 7 at the Afterpay Arena, the former champion isn’t in a hurry to get back inside the Octagon. Jack Della Maddalena Explains Why He’s Delaying UFC Return After Two Straight Losses In a recent interview with Bedtime MMA , Maddalena revealed that he was indeed offered a spot on the upcoming Sydney Fight Night card in February. However, he turned down the opportunity because he felt the proposed timeline was too short. He explained, “I do like traveling for fights. It is obviously awesome fighting in Australia. You get the whole crowd backing. But I feel definitely less pressure fighting elsewhere. The Sydney card would obviously be sick. It was a good opportunity. They did ask, but I feel like the last one, I sort of just jumped into the Perth fight because I kind of had to.” The former 170lbs champion added, “I didn’t want to get sucked in too early. My plan after the last fight was develop the skills, become a better martial artist, so I didn’t want to just jump just because of the location.” Following his one-sided loss to Prates, Maddalena wants to focus on improving his overall game before making his return, which he is targeting for April or May 2027. He said, “I wanted to give the best performance for the fans, for the team. (I’m) just going to ride it out a bit, but ready to go April, May next year.” Although he hasn’t looked like the same fighter who defeated Belal Muhammad at UFC 315 to capture the welterweight championship, Maddalena remains confident that his best days are still ahead of him. He said, “My best performances are in front of me, so this isn’t the end. This is just another speed bump, and we will be back.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by UFC Europe (@ufceurope) ALSO READ: Uros Medic Has a Surprising Suggestion for Islam Makhachev After Years of UFC Dominance Maddalena has every reason to believe he can turn things around. He actually began his professional MMA career with two consecutive losses before putting together an incredible 18-fight winning streak that eventually took him to the 170lbs throne. Now, he’ll be looking to rediscover that form when he finally returns. There are also several interesting matchups waiting for the Australian, with potential opponents including Shavkat Rakhmonov and Mike Malott. It remains to be seen who the UFC will line up for him, but Maddalena appears determined to take his time and get things right before stepping back into the Octagon.

item.title: Lakeview field hockey wins first Berkshire League tournament title on penalty strokes
item.description: The Lakeview field hockey team poses with the championship banner after beating Nonnewaug on penalty shots in the Berkshire League tournament final Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, at Nonnewaug High in Woodbury. (Cody Dzis/Hearst Connecticut Media) WOODBURY - Lakeview field hockey player Rowan Kinsella told head coach Ashley LaBonte she didn't want to take a penalty stroke in Tuesday's Berkshire League tournament final because she was nervous. After a confidence boost from LaBonte, Kinsella converted a retaken stroke to give Lakeview the lead in the shootout. Goalie Kylie Reynolds forced Nonnewaug's final attempt wide to clinch Lakeview's first Berkshire League tournament championship in program history, 2-1 on penalty strokes after a 1-1 tie through two overtimes. "What's funny is Rowan didn't even want to do it," LaBonte said. "She was so nervous going into it. I was like, ‘Yes, you can do this. I have faith in you,' and then she had to redo it. The girl that didn't want to do it at all had to redo it for a second time. The fact that she was the one that put us ahead was huge for her." "I honestly just blacked out, to be honest," Kinsella said. The referee called back Kinsella's first attempt because of goalie interference, forcing her to retake the stroke. "I went up, and I looked up and shot it and it was in the goal. I'm so happy we won and I'm so proud of this entire team." Reynolds, too, felt the nerves. "As a goalie, I have never seen a shootout before, so I was very nervous coming into it," Reynolds said. "Nonnewaug's a very strong team, but I was ready." Lakeview opened in fall 2024, following the merger of Litchfield Public Schools and Region 6 to form Region 20 Nonnewaug (13-2-3), the defending champion and No. 1 seed, advanced to the final with a 1-0 win over No. 4 Watertown last Thursday. Lakeview (12-5-1), the No. 2 seed, advanced with a 2-1 win over No. 3 Shepaug. Nonnewaug struck first with 5:28 left in the first quarter. Catherine Viveros scored off an assist from Lila Farrelly, giving the Chiefs a 1-0 lead. Lakeview couldn't convert its chances before halftime. Scozzafava made 23 saves in two regular-season shutouts against Lakeview. Before Tuesday, no Berkshire League opponent had scored against her. Lakeview finally broke through with 12:50 left in the third quarter. Christina Barone fought for the ball and scored to tie the game 1-1. "Our goal in this game was truly to score once because we knew [Scozzafava] had not had a goal scored against her from a Berkshire League team," LaBonte said. "Once we got that one, we were fired up, and these girls have worked so hard, have come together as a team, and it was a true team effort today." Lakeview pressed in the fourth quarter but couldn't take the lead. Neither team scored in the first 10-minute overtime. Barone had two chances in the second overtime, but Scozzafava saved one and the other went wide. The teams went to penalty strokes. Viveros scored for Nonnewaug in the shootout, while Bro

item.title: Buster Olney Thinks Seattle Mariners May Look To Offload Pitching Surplus
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 16: Bryan Woo #22 of the Seattle Mariners pitches the ball during the first inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on August 16, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Mariners have settled the biggest question of the offseason by hiring their new manager Jason Kanzler, but now the question of how they will go about trying to improve the roster comes to the fore. Buster Olney dropped a really interesting tidbit on what the Mariners may try to do in the offseason as it related to the team’s pitching surplus. Here is an excerpt from what Olney wrote: “I’ve heard Seattle is poking around to assess how its surplus in pitching might be used to add a bat.” However, he also stipulates that intense trade talks are probably not going to occur until after a new CBA is negotiated so teams have a better sense of what their financial situations are going to be. Still, it makes total sense for the Mariners to explore trading away a pitcher or two to try and improve the offense. Seattle was one of the worst teams in MLB offensively in 2026 and ranked 28th in runs per game. While the offense was poor, the Mariners have a lot of solid starting pitchers. Whether it’s Logan Gilbert, Bryan Woo, George Kirby, or Emerson Hancock, there is really no shortage of options if they want to thin things out a bit especially since Kade Anderson debuted and looked solid. Mariners should talk to teams in need of starting pitching Seattle would be wise to engage in talks with teams that are in desperate need of starting pitching. The Chicago Cubs make a lot of sense since basically their entire starting staff is set to hit free agency and they are bound to lose at least a couple of arms. Matt Shaw could be an interesting position player for the Mariners to target. The San Francisco Giants are another team that could use some starters. Logan Webb, Landen Roupp, and Adrian Houser should all be in the starting rotation but they have two spots that need filling. Maybe the Mariners could try to get Casey Schmitt who hit 21 home runs in 98 games last season. Another team to keep an eye on is the San Diego Padres . Michael King, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Nick Pivetta are all hitting free agency so they will likely need to replenish the rotation. Perhaps Jake Cronenworth or Xander Bogaerts could make sense as a boost to the lineup. Don’t expect any sort of deal this month like Olney said, but the Mariners are well-positioned to score a bat so they’d be foolish not to trade away a starter or two in order to improve on offense. item.title: ‘I Have Serious Concerns About Sam Darnold,’ ‘I Don’t Think Their Offense Is Good Enough’ — NFL Analysts React to Seahawks Losing 3 of Last 4 Games
item.description: 'I Have Serious Concerns About Sam Darnold,' 'I Don't Think Their Offense Is Good Enough' — NFL Analysts React to Seahawks Losing 3 of Last 4 Games The Seahawks were outplayed by the Chicago Bears, who not only dominated on the field but also had their fans make their presence felt at Lumen Field. The loss just served to rub salt in Seattle’s wounds, given that it has now lost three of its last four, leaving it at 4-4. With their position in the NFC playoff picture becoming increasingly precarious, these struggles have sparked discussions among several analysts, who shared their thoughts on the team’s sudden decline. NFL Analysts Split on Seahawks After Crushing Bears Defeat The Seahawks entered Monday’s game with a 21-6 record dating back to the beginning of last season, including their playoff appearances. However, their 34-17 loss against the Bears was unlike most of their previous losses, as they struggled in all three phases of the game. The loss ended the Seahawks’ 30-game run without losing a game by more than 4 points in the regular season or playoffs, in what served as their most lopsided loss in nearly two years, since Seattle had not suffered a loss by more than four points since Dec. 15, 2024. Seeing the Seahawks struggle, PFN analyst Ian Cummings believes Sam Darnold’s inconsistent performances could become a big problem despite the team’s defensive strength and offensive talent. “Very few teams can beat the attrition of an inconsistent, turnover-prone quarterback under center,” Cummings said. “The Seahawks still have an elite defense, and they still have star power on offense with players like Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Quenton Nelson up front, but Sam Darnold is firmly on regression watch.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer As Cummings noted, Darnold ranks outside the top 20 in PFN’s QB Impact Metric entering Week 9. Cummings also noted that Darnold has reduced his fumbles compared to 2025, but his interception rate has climbed to 4.3%, nearly matching his 4.7% touchdown rate. “Darnold’s contract actually makes re-assessment possible; he only signed a three-year deal with Seattle in 2025,” Cummings added. However, PFN analyst Jacob Infante is not particularly concerned about Seattle’s chances of reaching the playoffs. “I believe the NFC North will cannibalize itself to the point where, eventually, one of those teams works their way out of a Wild Card spot,” Infante said. “That said, Seattle has a lot of work to do if it is to re-establish itself as a legitimate Super Bowl contender. “The hope is that trading for Quenton Nelson and getting Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back healthy will help the Seahawks get their offense back on track. As it stands, though, I don’t think their offense is good enough to make a deep playoff run.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The Bears also exposed some weaknesses in Seattle’s defense from the opening possession.
